messages:
sam-infra: Heads up — seeing ~30 ALB target deregistrations from edge-pool-us-west-2 starting at 22:01 UTC. Health checks time out, then targets removed. Happens right after the egress NAT rule rollout. Anyone else seeing this?

maria-sre: Yep, saw the same. ALB logs show repeated "504 Gateway Timeout" for the probe path then deregister. Pod readiness probes are fine locally, but ALB -> pod times out.

lucy-edge: Quick snapshot of ALB logs: ```[2026-03-17T22:01:12Z] target=ip-10-0-5-21 health_check=timeout code=504 latency=10s``` repeated across many IPs.

sam-infra: kubectl describe shows readiness transitions: ```Readiness probe failed: Get http://10.0.5.21:8080/healthz: dial tcp 10.0.5.21:8080: i/o timeout``` so the connection from ALB to pod's node IP is timing out.

maria-sre: My hypothesis: ephemeral SNAT port reuse spike after the new egress rule changed how traffic is SNAT'd -> transient NAT port exhaustion/rotation leads to existing ALB healthcheck flows being dropped. This matches the rollout timing.

infra-automation-bot: deploy event: egress-nat-rules v3 deployed by @sam-infra at 2026-03-17T22:00:58Z.

lucy-edge: Quick checks we ran: on affected nodes `sudo conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` -> high counts (~18k) and `ss -s` shows high ephemeral port usage. Also saw kube-proxy restarts on a few nodes around the same time.

tim-oncall: Workarounds we can try now: 1) Scale out the edge node pool to reduce per-node SNAT pressure, 2) pin ALB health checks to nodePort instead of pod IPs temporarily, 3) roll back egress rule if the risk persists. Which do we want to do first?

sam-infra: I'm starting a small scale-up of the edge pool (+3 nodes) to see if that reduces removals. Rolling back egress rules is risky for ongoing infra changes but we can revert if scale-up doesn't help within 10m.

kyle-ml: Noted: jobs hitting GPUs on the same AZ might also be generating high outbound connections (data callbacks). I'll throttle a couple of training jobs in us-west-2 to drop overall NAT pressure.

maria-sre: Also recommend increasing the SNAT port range on nodes and bumping conntrack timeout for established flows as a medium-term fix. I'll open a follow-up ticket for the config change.

lucy-edge: Short term check command we used: ```# on node
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
# expected: widen port range to avoid reuse```

sam-infra: Scale-up showing early signs: ALB deregistrations have slowed in the last 90s. Still monitoring. If we see another wave we'll trigger rollback.

deploy-bot: INFO: canary-deploy/edge-egress v3 reported healthy after 60s.

maria-sre: Action items: - kyle throttle noncritical outbound jobs (in progress) - infra: prepare SNAT range bump + conntrack tuning (ticket: INF-5421) - ops: keep scale-up for 30m then re-evaluate.

sam-infra: Thanks all. I'll post an update in 15m with metrics. :thumbsup:
